site: Mount Sharp boxwork, Gale Crater, Mars

layers.name: Minerals (CRISM strip, about 16 km south of the route)

stops.name: Base
stops.hazard: Slope here is 6.5 degrees, under the 12 degree safety limit: walk normally.
stops.task: Check your suit and oxygen, then look ahead at the first ridges.
stops.science: Boxwork is a network of low ridges about 1 to 2 meters tall with sandy hollows between them; scientists think groundwater flowed through cracks in the rock and left minerals behind.

stops.name: First ridges
stops.hazard: Slope here is 9.9 degrees, under the 12 degree safety limit, but steeper than at base: walk carefully.
stops.task: Look closely at the ridge rock for small round bumps called nodules.
stops.science: Pea-sized bumps called nodules in the boxwork are minerals left behind by groundwater.

stops.name: Steep ridge
stops.hazard: Steep slope: 15 degrees, above the 12 degree safety limit. Walk slowly and watch your footing.
stops.task: Photograph the ridge from a safe spot; do not climb it.
stops.science: Samples NASA drilled from a boxwork ridge contained clay minerals.

stops.name: Hollow
stops.hazard: Slope here is 4.7 degrees, nearly flat. The hollows between ridges are sandy: test the ground before you step.
stops.task: Check the ground for loose sand before you step; do not rush.
stops.science: A sample NASA drilled from bedrock in a boxwork hollow contained carbonate minerals.

stops.name: Main site
stops.hazard: Slope here is 11 degrees, just under the 12 degree safety limit, and nearby points reach 12 to 14 degrees: watch your footing.
stops.task: Photograph the ridges and hollows around you and note anything unusual.
stops.science: Curiosity's main exploration of the boxwork ran from about sol 4600 to sol 4805, and this stop is inside that period.

stops.name: Exit
stops.hazard: Slope here is 3.7 degrees, nearly flat. Check your oxygen before the walk back to base.
stops.task: Take a last photo of the boxwork, then check your oxygen and start the walk back to base.
stops.science: Around sol 4805, Curiosity began its final phase in the boxwork: last measurements of ridges and hollows, and a look at where the boxwork meets the neighboring rock layers.
